lede.headline: Big Tech's earnings week splits the AI trade
lede.dek: Alphabet's profit miss sent its stock down more than 12%, even as Microsoft and Amazon posted their fastest cloud growth in years.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Alphabet profit misses as cloud revenue doubles
stories.move: Alphabet reported Q3 2026 revenue of $127.6 billion, up about 25% from a year earlier, with Google Cloud revenue roughly doubling to $30.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.12, below the $3.01 analysts expected. Shares fell more than 12% the next trading day.
stories.why: Investors focused on the earnings miss and rising AI infrastructure costs even though cloud growth accelerated sharply.
stories.bear: Cloud revenue growth of around 103% suggests the long-term AI buildout is paying off, and one quarter's EPS miss doesn't erase that trend.
stories.watch: Alphabet's next earnings report, expected in late January 2027.

stories.headline: Microsoft's Azure growth accelerates to 48%
stories.move: Microsoft reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19%, beating the roughly $90.7 billion analysts expected. Azure revenue grew 48% to $33.2 billion, the first time Microsoft has disclosed Azure's dollar figure rather than just a growth rate. Net income rose 32% to $36.6 billion, or $4.92 per diluted share.
stories.why: Azure's acceleration and the first-ever dollar disclosure gave investors a clearer read on how big the AI-driven cloud business has become.
stories.bear: Capital spending of $39.4 billion for the quarter, with full-year guidance near $175 billion, raises the bar for future quarters to keep justifying that spend.
stories.watch: Microsoft's fiscal second-quarter report, expected in late January 2027.

stories.headline: AWS posts its fastest growth in nearly five years
stories.move: Amazon reported Q3 2026 revenue of $201.9 billion, up 12%, with AWS revenue up 39% to $46 billion and AWS operating income of $17.8 billion, more than offsetting the prior year's $11.4 billion. Total operating income hit a record $28.1 billion, a 13.9% margin. Diluted EPS was $1.89, below the roughly $1.96 analysts expected, and advertising revenue of $19.6 billion also missed estimates.
stories.why: AWS's acceleration drove the headline strength, even as a smaller EPS and ad-revenue miss left some results mixed.
stories.bear: Amazon guided to only 12% to 16% sales growth for the current quarter, a wide range that leaves room for a holiday-season slowdown.
stories.watch: Amazon's Q4 holiday-quarter results, expected in early February 2027.

stories.headline: AMD to invest $1 billion in Meta's stock offering
stories.move: AMD said on October 27 it will invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering as part of an expanded AI infrastructure partnership. Meta has installed and is testing AMD's first Helios GPU rack systems, and AMD's EPYC chips support the computing behind Meta's Muse AI agent. Meta's stock sale was raised to $25 billion in common shares, priced at $625 each, a 2.7% discount to the prior close.
stories.why: AMD is tying itself closer to one of its largest AI infrastructure customers as Meta raises tens of billions for data centers.
stories.bear: AMD's own release didn't disclose a purchase price, share count or timing for its own stake, so the $1 billion commitment isn't a completed investment yet.
stories.watch: AMD's Q3 earnings report on November 3.

stories.headline: Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta's stock offering
stories.move: Nvidia said on October 26 it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering, alongside expanded joint work on Meta's Muse AI agent models. On Meta's earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg said Muse's user accounts had passed 10 million. Nvidia did not disclose the price or share count for its planned purchase.
stories.why: The investment deepens Nvidia's ties to one of its biggest AI infrastructure customers just as AMD expands its own footprint there.
stories.bear: Nvidia's stake is still a plan, not a completed purchase, and the company has disclosed no terms for it.
stories.watch: Whether Nvidia discloses purchase terms once Meta's offering closes.

stories.headline: Oracle sets $225 billion revenue target for 2030
stories.move: Oracle's co-CEOs and CFO told investors at an October 28 investor day the company targets $225 billion or more in total revenue by fiscal 2030, with non-GAAP operating margin of at least 40% and non-GAAP EPS of $21 or more. Oracle also committed to limiting new capital-markets funding through fiscal 2030 to $20 billion, split evenly between equity and debt. Shares rose about 10.7% that day.
stories.why: Oracle laid out a path to fund its AI data-center buildout mostly from its own growing cash flow rather than heavy new borrowing or stock sales.
stories.bear: The targets reach four years out, and Oracle still expects capital spending to peak before free cash flow turns solidly positive in fiscal 2029.
stories.watch: Oracle's fiscal second-quarter results, expected in December.

stories.headline: SoftBank-backed quantum project wins Japanese funding
stories.move: A materials-research project backed by SoftBank and five other Japanese companies - Toppan Holdings, Aisin, Asahi Kasei, AGC and DIC - was selected for funding by Japan's NEDO technology agency on October 28. The project, running through fiscal 2028, aims to combine quantum computing with AI screening to speed up materials research and development. SoftBank shares rose about 4.8% that day.
stories.why: The government-backed funding adds a new angle to SoftBank's AI bet beyond its existing stakes in Arm and OpenAI.
stories.bear: The platform's three-year commercialization goal is early-stage, and government-funded research projects don't guarantee a near-term payoff.
stories.watch: SoftBank's next earnings report, scheduled for November 10.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms lists in India's largest-ever IPO
stories.move: Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital arm of Reliance Industries, began trading on India's NSE and BSE on October 28 after raising ₹30,213 crore in India's largest IPO, subscribed 22.19 times. Shares priced at ₹1,119 opened at ₹1,358, a 21.36% premium, and closed the day at about ₹1,417, up 26.66%. The listing made Jio Platforms India's second most valuable listed company by market value, behind parent Reliance Industries.
stories.why: Strong demand for the offering reflects investor appetite for Reliance's telecom and digital business, valued separately from its energy and retail operations.
stories.bear: First-day pops often fade, and most of the proceeds - about ₹27,500 crore - go toward paying down the telecom unit's debt rather than new growth spending.
stories.watch: Jio Platforms' first quarterly results as a standalone listed company.

consensus.headline: Nvidia and AMD both buy into Meta's AI buildout
consensus.body: Nvidia and AMD each announced plans this week to invest in Meta's stock offering, a combined $4 billion, as Meta raises up to $95 billion to fund AI data centers.

watch: Apple reports fiscal Q4 results on November 2.
AMD reports Q3 earnings on November 3.
Arm Holdings reports fiscal second-quarter earnings on November 4.
Adobe's Shantanu Narayen hands the CEO role to Anil Chakravarthy on December 1.
memo: Cloud growth is still accelerating at Microsoft and Amazon - don't assume AI-driven capacity constraints from cloud vendors are easing soon.
Chipmakers are now investing cash directly into their biggest customers' stock offerings, a sign of how tightly AI infrastructure capital ties have become.
Oracle's plan to fund growth mostly from its own cash flow by 2029, rather than more debt or stock sales, is a tell that even AI leaders are watching their balance sheets.

movers.why: Oracle rose 10.7% after setting a $225 billion revenue target for fiscal 2030 at its investor day.
SoftBank rose 4.8% after a quantum-materials research project with five Japanese firms won government funding.
AMD rose 3.2% after Susquehanna raised its price target on the stock to $650.
